title: MyRecon vs BeenVerified: OSINT Tools Compared
description: Compare MyRecon and BeenVerified: search inputs, public workflows, and verification limits. Choose an OSINT tool for authorized research.
h1: MyRecon vs BeenVerified: compare public-search workflows
intro: Looking for a BeenVerified alternative depends on the task: BeenVerified is a subscription background-check and people-search service indexing commercial records, property deeds, and phone directories. MyRecon is a browser-based public username search and digital footprint audit tool. This page compares their workflows, ethics, and costs objectively.

sections.heading: What BeenVerified is designed to do
sections.body: BeenVerified is described as a commercial public records search engine that compiles background reports from government filings, property rolls, court registries, and consumer data aggregators. It operates on a recurring subscription model and focuses primarily on US-based identity records, contact details, and criminal history checks.

sections.heading: Where a MyRecon workflow fits
sections.body: MyRecon focuses specifically on public online footprints and open-source intelligence: checking usernames across 500+ social and developer platforms, discovering email data breaches, checking domain RDAP/DNS records, and helping users audit accounts they control. It requires no recurring subscriptions and does not compile personal background dossiers.

sections.heading: Compare evidence rather than promotional claims
sections.body: Commercial background services often market their reports with sensational claims. In contrast, open-source intelligence emphasizes direct verification: inspecting actual live profile URLs, checking k-anonymity breach records, and corroborating findings using independently documented evidence.

faq.question: Is MyRecon a free alternative to BeenVerified?
faq.answer: For username searches, social media footprint audits, and email breach lookups, yes. MyRecon offers free guest scans without recurring subscription paywalls. However, MyRecon does not provide US public records like criminal histories or property deeds.

faq.question: Does MyRecon sell personal information or contact details?
faq.answer: No. MyRecon queries live public endpoints to see if a handle exists, and does not sell marketing lists, phone numbers, or private dossiers.

faq.question: Can I remove my data from BeenVerified?
faq.answer: Yes. MyRecon publishes a step-by-step opt-out tutorial explaining how to submit an official opt-out request directly to BeenVerified.
